chunks: I have come to know of your strictness with Banū Tamīm and your harshness over them,
And indeed, Banū Tamīm are such that if one star sets, another rises for them,
And they were never exceeded in the art of war in pre-Islamic times or after Islam,
And they have a special kinship with us and a particular relationship,
We shall be rewarded if we pay heed to the kinship and be deemed sinful if we disregard it.
ai.seo_question: Why does Imam Ali emphasize the kinship of Banu Tamim in his letter to the governor of Basra?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) highlights the Banū Tamīm's enduring resilience and martial prowess, noting that their strength has never waned from the pre-Islamic era through Islam. He underscores their specific kinship with the Prophet's family (Ahl al-Bayt), framing the maintenance of this bond as a religious duty where reward is tied to connection and sin to severance. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *silat al-rahim* (maintaining kinship) as a spiritual imperative rooted in divine promise.
